title: Introduce temporal cohort consensus and stability oracle for rollout gating
author: Asha Kapoor
release_notes: Adds a cohort-aware consensus detector and a stability oracle that aggregates cross-cohort signals to produce a single pass/fail rollout gate; configurable hysteresis and traffic-hedging defaults included.
description:
Context and motivation: We observe frequent noisy short-lived latency blips in single traffic slices (region/hour/client-version) that cause over-sensitive canary rollbacks or false positives. Existing detectors either aggregate too aggressively (masking real regressions) or act on tiny cohorts (overreacting to noise). This change introduces a temporal cohort consensus algorithm and a stability oracle that combines cross-cohort agreement, signal persistence, and traffic-weighted impact to produce a single binary gate for automated rollouts.

What this PR does: 1) Implements a 'cohort engine' that slices traffic deterministically by features (region, hour-of-day bucket, client_signature) and computes per-cohort detection signals (latency/throughput delta quantiles). 2) Adds a consensus layer that computes agreement across cohorts using a probabilistic quorum: cohorts vote weighted by recent traffic and SLO sensitivity; the consensus score is mapped to an oracle decision with hysteresis. 3) Introduces a stability oracle service used by the rollout controller to accept/reject canary progressions and to decide hedging (auto-shift small percentages to baseline when consensus is borderline). 4) Adds configuration knobs: min_cohort_size, quorum_threshold, persistence_window, hedging_fraction, and slo_weighting_profile. 5) Bundles end-to-end tests and a new canary dashboard fragment for cross-cohort views.

Design notes (short): - Cohorts are stable slices computed from request attributes to avoid churn; a Bloom-filter-based sketch prevents combinatorial explosion. - Voting uses a Beta-regularized score to combine quantile shifts and variance, making the detector robust to low-sample cohorts. - Hysteresis is time-based (persistence_window) + effect-size guard (requires delta > min_effect for at least two quantiles). - Hedging triggers gradual traffic redistribution to baseline model if consensus is in the gray zone, reducing blast radius while keeping the canary alive for observation.

Commit summary: - a1b2c3: core cohort engine, cohort hashing, sketching, and per-cohort signal computation. - d4e5f6: consensus aggregator, quorum math, and stability oracle API. - 7g8h9i: rollout controller integration, hedging logic, and config schema. - j0k1l2: end-to-end synthetic perf tests, load generator scenarios, and CI harness updates. - m3n4o5: docs, console dashboard fragment, and migration notes.

Files changed (high-level): - src/detectors/cohort_engine.py (new) - src/detectors/consensus_aggregator.py (new) - src/oracle/stability_oracle_service.py (new) - src/controller/rollout_controller.py (modified: hedging integration + decision path) - infra/helm/canary-values.yaml (add config knobs) - tests/e2e/cohort_consensus_synth.py (new) - web/console/src/pages/canary/cohort-overview.tsx (new) - docs/perf/canary-cohort-consensus.md (new) - ci/perf-harness.yaml (modified) plus smaller utility and proto changes (config/README).

Review conversation (highlights, chronological single string): Reviewer Liam O'Connor: "Nice approach, cohort hashing sketch is neat. Two asks: (1) add doc explaining failure modes for low-sample cohorts, (2) ensure we don't introduce new high-cardinality tags accidentally." Author (Asha): "Added low-sample fallback and updated doc; cohort hash includes explicit allowlist and automatic cardinality guard." Reviewer Marcos Alvarez: "Quorum math looks plausible but can we add a simulation for skewed traffic (90/10) to ensure hedging doesn't starve baseline?" Author: "Added test scenario 'skewed_traffic_90_10' in e2e suite; hedging respects min_baseline_threshold." Reviewer Priya Raman: "We need observability hooks: emit cohort-level metrics and a consolidated consensus metric for the dashboard." Author: "Emitted metrics: cohort.vote_count, cohort.score, consensus.score, oracle.decision with tags. Added dashboard fragment." Reviewer tests: "LGTM after small nits"; Marcos approved, Priya requested one small change which was addressed.

CI summary: - unit tests: pass - linters: pass (fixed minor formatting) - perf-harness: ran synthetic nightlies; two transient flaky cases were retriggered and passed on rerun - integration: pass on staging. Overall CI_status: pass.

Performance and safety testing done: - 72-hour synthetic run with mixed traffic shapes (diurnal + regional bursts) demonstrating 3x reduction in false positives vs baseline detector. - Skewed traffic test (90% heavy, 10% light): hedging preserved baseline availability and avoided premature rollbacks. - Canary regression injection: real regressions (3–8% p95 increase) produced high consensus and fast automated rollback. - Load impact: cohort engine adds ~1.5% CPU at peak to aggregator nodes; memory footprint increase ~40MB per aggregator—within capacity targets.

Migration and config: - Default behavior is gated behind 'cohort_consensus.enabled = false' for 2 weeks; ops can flip in feature flags to enable experiment mode per environment. - Config knobs exposed in helm values: min_cohort_size, quorum_threshold (0.0-1.0), persistence_window_seconds, hedging_fraction, min_baseline_threshold. - Rollout plan: enable in dev -> staging (observability on) -> enable in canary-only on prod (week 1) -> gradual promotion.

Backward compatibility and risk: - No breaking API changes; proto extensions are additive. - Risk: increased complexity around cohort cardinality; mitigations: allowlist, sketch cardinality guard, and default conservative thresholds.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main on 2026-02-16 by Asha Kapoor (merge method: squash).

Follow-ups (future work): - Explore adaptive quorum that learns weights from historical SLO regressions. - Integrate cohort consensus into cross-region failover policy. - Expose per-cohort historical traces in console for postmortem.
